newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler CEO says vehicle forecast unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler CEO says vehicle forecast unchanged.

text.p: Chrysler Corp Chairman Robert Eaton said Wednesday that Chrysler's estimate for U.S. auto industry vehicle sales in 1997 remains unchanged at 15.2 to 15.5 million units, despite strong sales results in March.

Eaton, speaking to reporters at a Chrysler engine plant where he announced $1.3 billion in new investments in six Detroit facilities, said the March sales rate was not sustainable and was "a little stronger than I would like."
U.S. vehicle sales, including medium and heavy trucks, ran at a seasonally adjusted annual sales rate of about 16.1 million units in March.
Eaton said continued sales at that rate would likely bring additional actions by the Federal Reserve Board to increase interest rates.
"If that were to be sustained, we'd have additional interest rate increases, and that would tone the market down," he said.

But Fed would have to raise interest rates by another 75 basis points -- producing a full percentage point increase including its recent 25 basis-point hike -- in order to make a significant impact on U.S. vehicle sales, Eaton said.
"Another 25 basis points won't do it," he said.
Asked if Chrysler would attempt to counteract any negative effects of interest rate increases with higher incentives, he said the automaker would "do whatever we have to to remain competitive."

Chrysler on Tuesday announced that it would offer its first nationwide incentive on its minivan models since they were redesigned for the 1996 model year, a $595 rebate on vans with a left-side sliding door.
Eaton said he expected that Chrysler's overall incentive levels for the second quarter would be $100 to $150 per vehicle higher than in the first quarter.

Chrysler is scheduled to report its first quarter earnings on Thursday. According to First Call Corp., the consensus Wall Street analysts estimate for Chrysler is $1.43 a share, up from $1.31 a year earlier.
